Abstract: Organocatalytic dearomatization of β-
naphthols has been achieved via a 1,6-conjugated
addition of 2-naphthols to alkynyl 7-methylene-7H-
indoles in situ
generated from α-(7-
indolyl)methanols. In the presence of racemic
phosphoric acid, a series of tetrasubstituted allenes
was obtained in high yields. Particularly, with the
aid of chiral phosphoric acid, asymmetric dearoma-
tization of β-naphthols was investigated, affording
axially chiral tetrasubstituted allenes with moderate
enantioselectivity.
Keywords: Addition; Allenes; Dearomatization; In-
dolylmethanol; Organocatalysis
With cheap and convenient aromatic compounds as
starting materials, the catalytic dearomatization reac-
tions have paved a robust way to construct polycyclic
molecules with stereogenic centers.<sup>[1]</sup> Owing to the
significant advancements in asymmetric organocataly-
sis, notably chiral phosphoric acid catalysis,<sup>[2]</sup> organo-
catalytic dearomatization reactions of aromatic com-
pounds have witnessed remarkable progress.<sup>[3]</sup>
Particularly, readily available naphthols represent im-
portant platforms to construct intriguing 3D-molecular
complexity.<sup>[4]</sup> It is noteworthy that organocatalytic
enantioselective dearomatization reactions of naphthols
have been successfully developed to incorporate
stereogenic centers within the naphthyl skeletons via
the formation of new carbon-carbon and hetero-carbon
bonds, utilizing appropriate partners including
azodicarboxylates,<sup>[5]</sup> nitroethylene,<sup>[6]</sup> 1,3-dichloro-5,5-
dimethylhydantoin,<sup>[7]</sup>
quinones,<sup>[8]</sup>
quinone
monoimides,<sup>[9]</sup> N-(arylthio)succinimides and N-
(arylthio)phthalimides,<sup>[10]</sup> allenamides,<sup>[11]</sup> β,γ-alkynyl-
α-imino esters,<sup>[12]</sup> and o-quinone diimides.<sup>[13]</sup> Impor-
tantly, these impressive reactions provide efficient
access to enantioenriched naphthalenones.
Due to its unique chemical properties, the axial
chiral tetrasubstituted allene has garnered immense
interest and attention from the scientific community.<sup>[14]</sup>
Recently, α-indolylmethanols have emerged as versa-
tile building blocks in organic synthesis to construct
indole-based derivatives.<sup>[15]</sup> Specifically, with the aid
of chiral phosphoric acids (CPAs) or their analogues,
dehydration of these α-indolylmethanols in situ gener-
ated conjugate systems such as 2-methylene-2H-
indoles (Scheme 1A),<sup>[16]</sup>
3-methylene-3H-indoles
(Scheme 1B),<sup>[17]</sup>
6-methylene-6H-indoles
(Scheme 1C).<sup>[18]</sup> In contrast, the organocatalytic enan-
tioselective reactions of 7-methylene-7H-indoles
formed in situ from α-(7-indolyl)methanols
(Scheme 1D) remained underdeveloped and in an
immature state. In 2018, Mei and Shi et al. reported a
chiral phosphoric acid (CPA) catalyzed reaction of α-

naphthols has been achieved via a 1,6-conjugated
addition of 2-naphthols to alkynyl 7-methylene-7H-
indoles in situ
generated from α-(7-
indolyl)methanols. In the presence of racemic
phosphoric acid, a series of tetrasubstituted allenes
was obtained in high yields. Particularly, with the
aid of chiral phosphoric acid, asymmetric dearoma-
tization of β-naphthols was investigated, affording
axially chiral tetrasubstituted allenes with moderate
enantioselectivity.
Keywords: Addition; Allenes; Dearomatization; In-
dolylmethanol; Organocatalysis
With cheap and convenient aromatic compounds as
starting materials, the catalytic dearomatization reac-
tions have paved a robust way to construct polycyclic
molecules with stereogenic centers.<sup>[1]</sup> Owing to the
significant advancements in asymmetric organocataly-
sis, notably chiral phosphoric acid catalysis,<sup>[2]</sup> organo-
catalytic dearomatization reactions of aromatic com-
pounds have witnessed remarkable progress.<sup>[3]</sup>
Particularly, readily available naphthols represent im-
portant platforms to construct intriguing 3D-molecular
complexity.<sup>[4]</sup> It is noteworthy that organocatalytic
enantioselective dearomatization reactions of naphthols
have been successfully developed to incorporate
stereogenic centers within the naphthyl skeletons via
the formation of new carbon-carbon and hetero-carbon
bonds, utilizing appropriate partners including
azodicarboxylates,<sup>[5]</sup> nitroethylene,<sup>[6]</sup> 1,3-dichloro-5,5-
dimethylhydantoin,<sup>[7]</sup>
quinones,<sup>[8]</sup>
quinone
monoimides,<sup>[9]</sup> N-(arylthio)succinimides and N-
(arylthio)phthalimides,<sup>[10]</sup> allenamides,<sup>[11]</sup> β,γ-alkynyl-
α-imino esters,<sup>[12]</sup> and o-quinone diimides.<sup>[13]</sup> Impor-
tantly, these impressive reactions provide efficient
access to enantioenriched naphthalenones.
Due to its unique chemical properties, the axial
chiral tetrasubstituted allene has garnered immense
interest and attention from the scientific community.<sup>[14]</sup>
Recently, α-indolylmethanols have emerged as versa-
tile building blocks in organic synthesis to construct
indole-based derivatives.<sup>[15]</sup> Specifically, with the aid
of chiral phosphoric acids (CPAs) or their analogues,
dehydration of these α-indolylmethanols in situ gener-
ated conjugate systems such as 2-methylene-2H-
indoles (Scheme 1A),<sup>[16]</sup>
3-methylene-3H-indoles
(Scheme 1B),<sup>[17]</sup>
6-methylene-6H-indoles
(Scheme 1C).<sup>[18]</sup> In contrast, the organocatalytic enan-
tioselective reactions of 7-methylene-7H-indoles
formed in situ from α-(7-indolyl)methanols
(Scheme 1D) remained underdeveloped and in an
immature state. In 2018, Mei and Shi et al. reported a
chiral phosphoric acid (CPA) catalyzed reaction of α-
(7-indolyl)methanols with tryptamines for the synthesis
of structurally diversified chiral 7-indolylmethanes
(Scheme 2A).<sup>[19]</sup> Similarly, Antilla et al. also disclosed
a CPA-catalytic formal substitution of α-(7-
indolyl)methanols
with
aromatic
partners
(Scheme 2B).<sup>[18a]</sup> Notably, with aromatic amines as
nucleophiles, we have established a CPA- catalytic
aza-1,4-addition of 7-methylene-7H-indoles formed
in situ from α-(7-indolyl)methanols (Scheme 2C).<sup>[20a]</sup>
Furthermore, we also realized a CPA-catalyzed enan-
tioselective 1,6-addition of tryptamines to in situ
generated alkynyl 7-methylene-7H-indoles from the
corresponding α-(7-indolyl)propargylic alcohols, af-
fording axially chiral tetrasubstituted allenes featuring
indole and hexahydropyrrolo[2,3-b]indole units.<sup>[20b]</sup> As
a part of our continued interest in the field of
organocatalytic enantioselective reactions of α-func-
tionalized alcohols,<sup>[21]</sup> here we disclosed a phosphoric
acid catalyzed dearomatization reaction of β-naphthols
with alkyne 7-methylene-7H alcohols generated from
α-(7-indolyl)propargylic alcohols (Scheme 2D). Impor-
tantly, this protocol not only achieves the dearomatiza-
tion of β-naphthols but also enriches the chemistry of
α-(7-indolyl)methanols.

The investigation began with a model reaction
between α-(7-indolyl)propargylic alcohol 1 a and 1-
methyl-2-naphthol 2 a in dichloromethane (CH Cl ) at
room temperature for 16 h. As shown in Table 1, trace
of the desired product (+ /�)-3 aa was obtained from
the benzoic acid (PhCO H) catalyzed reaction (Ta-
ble 1, entry 1). To our delight, the p-toluenesulfonic
acid (TsOH) catalyzed reaction afforded the product
(+ /�)-3 aa in 46% yield (Table 1, entry 2). Notably,
the product (+/�)-3 aa was obtained in 58% yield
when racemic RPA-1 was employed as catalyst
(Table 1, entry 3). The next screening of solvents
(Table 1, entries 4–11) identified that trichloromethane
was suitable reaction media and enabled the formation
of the product (+ /� )-3 aa in 86% yield (Table 1,
entry 5).
Further modification of the reaction parameters,
including reaction temperature (Table 1, entry 12),
catalyst loading (Table 1, entry 13), and reactant ratio
(Table 1, entry 14), did not afforded better results.

Having the optimal conditions in hand, we exam-
ined the substrate scope of RPA-1 catalyzed reactions
(Table 2). Firstly, the range of α-(7-indolyl)propargylic
alcohols 1 was investigated by RPA-1 catalyzed
reaction of 1-methyl-2-naphthol 2 a (Table 2A). In
general, a broad range of α-(7-indolyl)methanols is
compatible, providing the corresponding adducts in
high yields. Specifically, the substituent R<sup>1</sup>/R<sup>2</sup> with
electron-withdrawing (F, Cl, and Br) or electron-
donating (Me and MeO) groups slightly affected the
yield, affording the corresponding products (+ /�)-
3aa-3ka, (+ /� )-3 na-3 ta in 70–86% yields. Impor-
tantly, neither significant electronic effects nor steric
hindrance effects were observed. Moreover, α-(7-
indolyl)methanol 1 l with heteroaromatic substituent
(R<sup>1</sup> = Ph, R<sup>2</sup> = 2-thienyl) was also tolerated, affording
the product (+ /�)-3 la in a yield of 70%. Exception-
ally, trace of product (+ /�)-3 ma was obtained from
the RPA-1 catalyzed reaction of α-(7-indolyl)methanol
with aliphatic substituents (R<sup>1</sup> = Ph, R<sup>2</sup> = cyclopropyl).
Subsequently, we investigated the substrate range of β-
naphthol (Table 2B). It was observed that the substitu-
ent R<sup>3</sup> exerted a pronounced impact on the yield.
Substituting the methyl group with alternative groups
such as ethyl, n-butyl (n-Bu), and benzyl (Bn), led to
suboptimal yields, affording the corresponding prod-
ucts (+ /�)-3 ab-ad in 50–73% yield. Particularly, 1-
phenyl-2-naphthol 2e was found to be incompatible
under the established reaction conditions.

reaction was scaled up to 2.0 mmol under the standard
conditions, the desired product of (+ /�)-3 aa was

In addition, we performed a preliminary survey of
the organocatalytic enantioselective version of this 1,6-
addition reaction (Table 3). A series of BINOL-derived
chiral phosphoric acids (CPAs) were examined via the
model reaction between α-(7-indolyl)propargylic alco-
hol 1a and 1-methyl-2-naphthol 2a in dichloromethane
at room temperature (Table 3, entries 1–12). To our
delight, all these CPAs could catalyze the reaction to
furnish chiral product. In particular, CPA-2 enabled
the formation of the desired chiral tetrasubstituted
allene 3aa in 69% yield with 43% ee and > 20:1 dr
(table 3, entry 2). In order to improve the enantiose-
lectivity, investigations on the effect of reaction media
were carried out (Table 3, entries 13–19). Notably,
toluene was identified as the most suitable reaction
medium to obtain product 3aa in 80% yield and 60%
ee and > 20:1 dr (Table 3, entry 15). To further
improve enantioselectivity, we modified the reaction
parameters including additives, temperature, and con-
centration, and no better results were obtained (Ta-
ble 3, entries 20–23). Although the enantioselectivity
was moderate, these preliminary results demonstrated
the possibility of constructing tetrasubstituted allene.

hol 1a and 1-methyl-2-naphthol 2a in dichloromethane
at room temperature (Table 3, entries 1–12). To our
delight, all these CPAs could catalyze the reaction to
furnish chiral product. In particular, CPA-2 enabled
the formation of the desired chiral tetrasubstituted
allene 3aa in 69% yield with 43% ee and > 20:1 dr
(table 3, entry 2). In order to improve the enantiose-
lectivity, investigations on the effect of reaction media
were carried out (Table 3, entries 13–19). Notably,
toluene was identified as the most suitable reaction
medium to obtain product 3aa in 80% yield and 60%
ee and > 20:1 dr (Table 3, entry 15). To further
improve enantioselectivity, we modified the reaction
parameters including additives, temperature, and con-
centration, and no better results were obtained (Ta-
ble 3, entries 20–23). Although the enantioselectivity
was moderate, these preliminary results demonstrated
the possibility of constructing tetrasubstituted allene.
In summary, we developed an organocatalytic
dearomatization of β-naphthols via an 1,6-conjugated
addition of alkynyl 7-methylene-7H-indoles in situ
generated from α-(7-indolyl)propargylic alcohols to
synthesize axially chiral tetrasubstituted allenes. Using
this method, a series of tetrasubstituted allenes were
obtained in high yields. Based on this foundation, we
delved into the exploration of the reaction’s enantiose-
lectivity and subsequently confirmed the practicality of
achieving such enantioselectivity. We expect this study
to stimulate more efforts to develop the enantioselec-
tive dearomatization of β-naphthols and enrich the
chemistry of α-(7-indolyl)methanols and axially chiral
tetrasubstituted allenes.
Experimental Section
To a solution of CHCl (0.3 mL) was added α-(7-
indolyl)propargylic alcohols 1 (0.075 mmol), 2-naphthols 2
(0.05 mmol), and RPA-1 (0.0025 mmol). The reaction mixture
was stirred at room temperature for 16 h, and then the solvent
was removed under vacuum to give a residue, which was
purified by silica gel chromatography to yield the desired
